drivers.variant_notes: Williams LA-5 production game ROMs (sstn_u26.l5, sstn_u27.l5) with the L-1 sound ROMs, the only Space Station driver in the pinned catalog (src/wpc/s11games.c lines 486-498; catalogued 1988, the year the manual was printed, while IPDB dates the first units December 7, 1987). The local archive's members match the driver's SHA-1s, and the retained known-working table binds it (cGameName = "spstn_l5"). Its lamp test is written for the "Wheel Version" backbox insert (see lamps 37, 41, 46-49 and 57); the same ROM runs both production insert boards.

The manual's Game Control Locations and Test/Diagnostic Procedures drive every test from the coin-door ADVANCE button and AUTO-UP/MANUAL-DOWN switch, and name the CPU board's SW 2 the CPU Diagnostic switch and its SW 1 the Sound Diagnostic switch. The retained runs enter and step the tests with -6 and -7.

Printed switch-matrix column 5 (GRN-BLK), row 1 (WHT-BRN). The ROM's Switch Levels test names it "R SNGLE DROP TG". The Switch-Matrix Table prints "Single Drop Target (right ramp)". The Switches parts list prints "Right1-bank Dr Tgt Opto". The manual identifies it as an optotransistor (C-11903-R 1-Bank Drop Target Opto Switch Assembly): each opto interrupter switches a 2N3906 PNP transistor onto the matrix row and column, per the amendment sheet's schematic. The matrix sees that transistor, which by the read-path rule stated below rests open, whatever the beam does. In the gameplay run the ROM fired the single drop-target reset (8) about 24 s after this address went to 1, at the end of the Stop 'N' Score timer the target starts, and retried every 1.4 s while it stayed at 1, so public 1 is the dropped target. In the ROM's Switch Levels test (run switch-levels) holding public 33 at 1 makes the player 1 and 2 displays show the ROM's name for it and the player 3 display its number, so the ROM reads it active at 1. spstnGameData has no inverted-switch mask and pia4a_r returns core_getSwCol raw, so the contact the matrix sees is open at rest and closed when actuated. The Switch-Matrix Table prints "(German Score Board Sw)" and the Switches parts list "(German Scoreboard)" with no part number: a switch of the scoreboard the West German version carries (the manual cuts jumper W7 for West German games). The L-5 ROM, the only pinned driver, names the address "NOT USED", so on this firmware nothing reads it; the West German machines' own game ROM is not in the pinned catalog. No source describes the switch's construction, polarity or location, so it is optional, without a normally-closed assertion or a placement.

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(55,56) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. S11.VBS names this address swURFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged right-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(3) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sURFlipper = 34) unless the table calls NoUpperRightFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleRFlip as a number other than True. The constant does not follow the PinMAME column, and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(55,56) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 56 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 56: a host write to 56 is overwritten on the next update. The retained known-working script drives it: Table1_KeyDown and Table1_KeyUp pass the right flipper key to S11.VBS vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp (script lines 1063 and 1086), which set Controller.Switch(swLRFlip) with swLRFlip = 82. In the Switch Levels run holding this address showed "RIGHT FLIPPER" with the number 56 and raised the synthetic outputs 45 and 46. The physical counterpart is the right cabinet flipper button (SW-10A-48), which fires the flipper coil through the flipper circuit and carries the Lane Change switch 56.

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Left End-of-Stroke (83)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLLFLIPEOSBIT = 0x04, published at 83 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(55,56) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. S11.VBS names this address swULFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged left-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(2) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sULFlipper = 36) unless the table calls NoUpperLeftFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleLFlip as a number other than True. The constant does not follow the PinMAME column, and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

System 11's single Country jumper, read via core_getDip(0)<<7 on PIA2 PA7 (pinned s11.c labels it "Jumper W7"). The manual's ROM and Jumper Table lists the CPU board's installed jumpers (W1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, 14, 16, 17, and 19), and its Circuit Boards text says "(Jumper W7 is cut/removed for West German games.)"

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball rolls onto the outhole switch (10, 17-1067) and the Outhole Kicker (1, AE-23-800) kicks it into the trough, where up to three balls queue on Ball Trough #3 (13, left), #2 (12) and #1 (11, right; the ROM's TROUGH BALL 1-3). The Ball Shooter Lane Feeder (2, C-9638-3 with an AE-23-800 coil) kicks the lead ball into the shooter lane, whose switch (43, the ROM's PLUNGER) the ball rests on until plunged; a wire habitrail carries the plunged ball to the 1-2-3 mini-playfield. With 10 held from power-up the ROM fired the outhole kicker every 2.2 s; in the gameplay run it fed the first ball at Start and repeated the feed 2.1 s later until a trough switch opened, served a new ball for each ball docked in a lock, and kicked the outhole 0.6 s after the drain. With no ball in the trough at power-up the ROM runs a ball search through 17, 32, 4 and 3; in play it searches through 3, 4, 13, 1, 8, 2 and the docks. The retained script models the trough with kickers sw10-sw13 and a cascade timer.
mechanisms.label: Outhole, three-ball trough and shooter-lane feeder

mechanisms.behavior: A raised translucent-blue mini-playfield (R-11780, 03-8109) at the top left takes the plunged ball and the ball the right popper lifts. Its three lanes 1 (14), 2 (15) and 3 (16) (5647-12073-01 switches on the A-11991 Switch & Diode Assy, lamps 14-16, the ROM's ROLOVER and UPPER LAMP 1-3) feed past two ball gates (B-11861, B-11788) onto the main playfield. Three lanes U (38), S (39) and A (40) run underneath it, reached by the shot round the left and back of the playfield past the Top Left Roll-Under (37); completing U-S-A advances the Stop 'N' Score multiplier and 1-2-3 the jet bumper value (rulesheet). IPDB pictures an opaque black prototype mini-playfield with leaf switches.
mechanisms.label: 1-2-3 mini-playfield and U-S-A lanes

mechanisms.behavior: The Space Station Wheel (03-8123) and the Rotating Ball Guide (03-8107) sit above the playfield at the top right on a shaft turned by the 14-7941-2 motor (24 VAC, 11 rpm) below it. Controlled solenoid 16 energizes the relay on the C-11902-1 relay board that runs the motor, in one direction only; the Wheel Positioner Cam (03-8106) on the shaft interrupts the two optos of the C-11872 Opto Positioner Board (OPTO 1 and OPTO 2), read as Space Station #1 (52) and #2 (53). The guide sends a ball arriving from the right ramp (through 46 on the station exit ramp) or lifted by the left popper (41, solenoid 3) to the right lock (45) or, over the wire ramp past 48, to the left lock (47). Per the rulesheet the ROM turns the station so that a ramp shot goes to an empty lock, and holds a ball in the left popper while it turns the station when one ball is already locked. At power-up the ROM energizes 16 and stops it on the edge into (52 open, 53 closed), whether the modelled cam reached it through (1,0) and (1,1) or straight from (0,0), and gives up after about 5.3 s when the switches never change; in the gameplay run, with both switches held open, it kept the motor running from Start until both locks emptied 90 s later. The physical cam profile is not printed. The retained known-working script, tested side by side with a real machine, models one revolution as two half-turn opto bits in quadrature (52 closed from 180 to 360 degrees, 53 closed from 90 to 270, starting at 90) with the guide sending balls left at 0 and 180 degrees and right at 90 and 270; a recreation that answers the ROM with that pattern satisfies the power-up homing seen here.
mechanisms.label: Space Station rotating ball guide

mechanisms.behavior: Two D-11335-1 Ball Popper Assemblies (vertical up-kickers) under the top of the playfield. The left popper (41, SW-1A-167, kicked by 3 with an AE-24-900 coil), which the rulesheet calls the centre popper, takes the shot round the left and back past the U-S-A lanes and lifts the ball to the Space Station, which guides it to a lock; it awards 100,000 when lit (lamp 36) and starts multiball with two balls locked. The right popper (42, kicked by 4, AE-23-800), reached past the drop targets, lifts the ball to the mini-playfield. In the gameplay run the ROM fired 4 0.45 s after 42 closed, and with 41 held while both locks were full it started multiball ("PILOT ONE ... LAUNCH PROBES") before lifting the ball. With both popper switches held from power-up it fired each every 2.2 s. An owner reports an artwork hole in front of a popper for a prototype drop target, which IPDB pictures.
mechanisms.label: Left (centre) and right ball poppers

mechanisms.behavior: Two ball locks the game calls docks. The right lock (45, the ROM's RIGHT LOCK UP) is kicked out by the Right Dock Kickback (17, Special #1, AE-23-800), which the Maintenance Information describes as the Right Eject Hole device using the shooter-lane feeder's mechanism; its entry switch (46, SW-1A-164) sits on the station exit ramp. The left lock (47, the ROM's LEFT LOCK UP) is kicked out by the Left Dock Kickbig (32, switched 08C, the B-11051-R Kickbig Arm Assembly with an AE-23-800 coil), and its entry switch (48) sits on the wire ramp. Docking W/L lamps 8 (left) and 34 (right) show which dock holds a ball; Docked Port Side (43) and Docked Starboard Side (45) light for a docked ball. In the gameplay run docking the right lock showed DOCKED RIGHT and the left DOCKED LEFT, each served a new ball, and the multiball release kicked the docks. At power-up the ROM kicks each once in its ball search; with 47 held it kept kicking 32 every 2.1 s, while with 45 held it kicked 17 only once more.
mechanisms.label: Left and right locks (docks)

mechanisms.behavior: A ramp on the right of the playfield carries the ball up to the Space Station; a single drop target (C-11212-2 Single-Bank Drop Target Assembly, C-11903-R opto board, switch 33) stands in front of its entrance and is raised by the Right Single Drop Target Reset (8, AE-23-800). Knocking it down starts Stop 'N' Score; a ramp shot before the timer runs out scores the counting value (lamp 33 STOP 'N' SCORE). In the gameplay run the ROM raised the target about 24 s after it went down and retried every 1.4 s while it stayed down. Owners report clear and black ramps; the production ramp is black.
mechanisms.label: Right ramp and its single drop target (Stop 'N' Score)

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets (C-11223-1, 03-8036 blades) sensed by the optos of a C-11318 opto switch assembly and reset together by the AE-26-1200 coil (6). Completing the bank advances the end-of-ball bonus multiplier (lamps 11-13 1X/2X/4X; the gameplay run showed 2X BONUS) and, at the adjusted multiplier, lights Extra Ball (lamp 5). In the gameplay run the ROM fired the reset once all three were held down and once more 1.3 s later.
mechanisms.label: 3-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: A bell-armature kicker (B-11873-1, AE-24-900 coil, solenoid 13) at the left drain lane (17), the left outlane of a machine with no inlanes, returns a draining ball to play while lamp 17 RE-ENTRY W/LIT is lit (lit at the start of a ball at the factory setting). In the gameplay run the ROM fired it within one poll of 17 closing. Lamp 32 RE-ENTRY W/LIT marks the right drain lane (32), which has no kicker. The retained script fires a VPX Kickback object.
mechanisms.label: Left re-entry kickback

mechanisms.behavior: Three jet bumpers (B-9414 above, B-9415-1 coil assemblies below, SW-11A-35 skirt switches): Left (21, switch 60), Right (19, switch 61) and Lower (22, switch 62). They are special solenoids whose circuits fire the coil from the bumper's own switch; spstnGameData mirrors that in PinMAME through sxx.ssSw, so each coil address rises with its switch while 23 is on. The wiring fold-out calls 21 the CENTER JET BUMPER.
mechanisms.label: Three jet bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Two kicker arm assemblies (B-9463, AE-26-1200 coils) above the flippers: Left (18, scoring switch 63) and Right (20, scoring switch 64). The Switches list footnote gives each a separate Kicker Actuating Switch (A-4834-H; B-8734 w/RC) with no matrix address. As special solenoids, each rises with its scoring switch through sxx.ssSw.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Two lower flippers (C-11626-R-4 and -L-4, FL-11630-50VDC coils). The cabinet buttons (SW-10A-48) fire the coils through the flipper circuit, so no Sol. No. or driver is printed for them and PinMAME fabricates 45-48 from the buttons at public 82 and 84. Each button also closes a Lane Change switch (55 left, 56 right) for the CPU, which core_updateSw copies from 84 and 82; the end-of-stroke switches in the coil circuit have no matrix address.
mechanisms.label: Two flippers, cabinet-wired

mechanisms.behavior: Seven B-11696-5 standups on the left spell SHUTTLE (18-24, lamps 18-24), three in the centre and four on the right spell STATION (25-31, lamps 25-31), and the B-11696-8 CHANGE bullseye target (35) changes the randomised SHUTTLE or STATION award shown on the two ladders of seven inserts in the middle of the playfield (lamps 50-56 and 58-64, with Change Shuttle 9 and Change Station 10). Two B-4834-K-1 10-point rubber switches sit at the top right (50) and lower right (54).
mechanisms.label: SHUTTLE and STATION standups, Change target and 10-point switches

mechanisms.behavior: Three relays (5580-09555-01 on C-11998-1 relay boards) switch the general illumination: 9 the playfield's white G.I., 10 between the white string and a second string of green bulbs, and 11 the backbox insert board's G.I. Energizing 9 or 11 turns its G.I. off (the ROM holds both through a tilt) and energizing 10 selects green, which the ROM does during multiball. PinMAME types all three as reverse-acting AC G.I. outputs.
mechanisms.label: White, green and insert-board G.I. relays

mechanisms.behavior: The A/C Select Relay (12) on the D-11813 Aux Power Driver Board switches each of the eight switched drivers (Q22-Q25, Q30-Q33) between its "A" load, while it is released, and its "C" load, while it is energized. Pinned PinMAME publishes the C loads separately at 25-32.
mechanisms.label: A/C solenoid select relay

mechanisms.behavior: The A-side load of pair 07 (7, AE-26-1200) raps the B-10686-2 Knocker Assembly in the backbox; the table allows a ticket dispenser in its place.
mechanisms.label: Backbox knocker

physical.notes: Solenoid Table entry 09 ("General Illum Relay (Playfield)"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "Gen. Illumin. Relay, P'field*". Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 16 of 28 while the player 1 and 2 displays show "PLAYFLD GEN ILU". The wiring fold-out (printed page 69) draws it in a 25 V frame. In the gameplay run the ROM energized it, with 11, from the third plumb-bob tilt until the next ball started, and flickered it for display effects. Retained script: SolModCallback GIUpdates (line 1103), which sets every playfield G.I. light (collections GI and gi_green) to the modulated level. The relay (5580-09555-01 on a C-11998-1 relay board under the playfield, the table's note 4) switches the playfield's white general illumination. Energized means G.I. off: the ROM holds it through a tilt, and pinned PinMAME types it as a reverse-acting #44 "GI output", so its modulated state is the brightness of the string the released relay feeds. The manual prints no G.I. bulb count or layout. The placements are the 51 playfield G.I. bulb lights of the retained table's two collections, the 26 white ones (GI) and the 25 green ones (gi_green), which GIUpdates sets together from this output; a table's G.I. grouping is not the machine's wiring, so they stay observed and no quantity is asserted.

Solenoid Table entry 10 ("General Illum Relay (Green)"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "Gen. Illumin. Relay, Green*". Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 17 of 28 while the player 1 and 2 displays show "PLAYFLD GRN GI". The wiring fold-out (printed page 69) draws it in a 25 V frame. In the gameplay run the ROM energized it 4.5 s after the left popper started multiball with both locks full and released it 8 s later, as the locked balls left. Retained script: GiSelect (line 1104), which shows the white G.I. light maps while it reads on and the green ones while it reads off. The relay (5580-09555-01 on a second C-11998-1 relay board under the playfield) switches the playfield G.I. between its white bulbs and a second string of green bulbs: IPDB's "Double GI - General Lighting changes from white to green during multiball" and an owner's "secondary GI circuit of green bulbs that comes on during multiball". The ROM energized it at multiball (see the gameplay run above), so energized is green.
